text:
Maya: Heads-up — seeing 95th+ tail spikes from eu-west in the evening when cross-zone routing is allowed. Spikes correlate with batches that opportunistically pull long-sequence requests after KV cache misses. Thinking we should adjust continuous-batching's late-bind window and region soft-reserve logic.

Tariq: Can you paste the flamegraph / perf counters? Do you mean increase late-bind wait or prefer local affinity unless capacity < X? Also thinking kernel-selection hysteresis so we don't thrash kernels on transient shape changes.

Devon: Quick profiling snippet from the spike window (attached in staging logs): KV hit-rate drops ~92% -> ~57% when spill occurs; avg tokens/request up ~30%. Shows a lot of long-seq requests entering already-started batches.

Devon: ```
queue.policy: soft_affinity
late_bind_ms: 6
min_batch_tokens: 32
region_token_budget: 5000
spill_threshold_pct: 0.15
// observed during spike: late_bind_ms=6 was too small for small bursts
```

infra-bot: loadtest result for experiment cand-config-7: p95 latency -12%, p99 latency +6% (eu-west) — more variance but lower mid-tail. See /staging/logs/1899987654.

Maya: That matches. My hypothesis: when a local GPU's KV cache is cold for some shard, we end up pulling cross-zone requests into in-progress batches because late-bind window is too aggressive for those long sequences. We should try: 1) increase late-bind for sequences > 256 tokens, 2) add a soft-regional token budget that biases routing to local until budget is low, 3) kernel hysteresis to avoid switching optimized kernels mid-batch.

Tariq: Proposed config to try in canary: bucketized token budgets per region (low/med/high), late-bind 6ms -> 14ms for seq>256, and kernel-hysteresis threshold 5000 tokens. Also add a probabilistic spillback gate so we don't fully block cross-zone during demand spikes.

Devon: I can run KV-cache focused profiling with synthetic long-seq traces and measure hit-rate with those configs. Will also record chain-of-batches to see how many batches get contaminated by late arrivals.

Maya: Action items: @Tariq implement config toggle + probabilistic spillback; @Devon run KV profiling and collect flamegraphs for eu-west/eu-central; I'll schedule a 2h canary tonight (22:00 UTC) and monitor p95/p99 and kernel-switch counts.

Tariq: I'll put a feature-flagged rollout (staging -> canary) and add telemetry: per-region token_budget_consumed, late_bind_samples, kernel_switches.

infra-bot: Canary scheduled: start=1899990000 (22:00 UTC), duration=7200s. Flag: candidate/cand-config-7. Metrics dashboard link: https://console.redwood.example/canary/1899990000

Maya: Good. If p99 regresses on canary we'll rollback immediately. Please add automated smoke that fails the canary if p99 > baseline +10% or kernel_switch_rate > baseline*1.5.

Devon: Noted. I'll include a KV-warmup preload test too to simulate steady-state.

Tariq: One more thought — maybe add a tiny local queue delay only when KV-hit-rate < threshold (e.g., 70%) to give local cache a chance to service miss backfills before spilling. That is, conditional late-bind. Might reduce unnecessary cross-zone transfers.

Maya: Love that. Conditional late-bind + bucketized budgets + kernel hysteresis. Let's keep the experiment narrow.

Devon: I'll update the test harness and push results to the canary doc.

Maya: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
